claim: Meta Louisiana / Hyperion data center expansion reached 5GW and $50B+ planned investment.
why_it_matters: Determines whether datacenter power and physical capacity are the primary scarce layer.
expected_confirming_evidence: Official MW capacity, capex amount, construction schedule, and power connection timeline.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: Project size lower than claimed, delayed timeline, no official confirmation, or capex not tied to AI capacity.

claim: Google 2026 capex guidance is materially higher because of AI infrastructure needs.
why_it_matters: Tests whether hyperscaler AI capex is accelerating and whether returns must be validated against Search, Cloud, and Gemini monetization.
expected_confirming_evidence: Management confirms higher capex tied to AI infrastructure and provides cloud or AI revenue support.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: Capex claim is not official, capex is lower, or AI monetization does not support the spending path.

claim: Amazon and other Big Tech issuers raised debt to fund AI capex.
why_it_matters: Tests whether AI buildout is becoming balance-sheet and financing constrained.
expected_confirming_evidence: Debt issuance is tied to AI infrastructure or datacenter capex and interest/debt metrics are material.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: Debt was not related to AI capex or the financing impact is immaterial.

claim: HBM / DRAM tightness is improving pricing power for Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung.
why_it_matters: Determines whether memory is a real scarce layer and whether earnings can be revised upward.
expected_confirming_evidence: Management reports HBM mix expansion, tight allocation, pricing strength, and margin improvement.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: Pricing weakens, inventory rises, HBM capacity expands faster than demand, or margins fail to improve.

claim: TSM is a health check for the AI chip cycle through advanced node and advanced packaging demand.
why_it_matters: Tests whether AI chip demand is confirmed by the upstream foundry gatekeeper.
expected_confirming_evidence: TSM confirms strong AI/HPC demand, tight advanced packaging capacity, and sustained capex tied to AI customers.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: TSM commentary shows AI demand slowing, packaging not tight, or capex being reduced.

claim: Advanced packaging, networking, optical interconnect, and compute-tray reliability are becoming bottlenecks in AI cluster deployment.
why_it_matters: Determines whether alpha is migrating from GPUs to enabling infrastructure layers.
expected_confirming_evidence: Companies report AI-specific design wins, backlog growth, pricing power, or deployment constraints tied to interconnect/reliability.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: No AI-specific revenue, weak backlog, low margin pass-through, or customer adoption delays.

claim: Hyperscaler AI capex may pressure FCF, depreciation, and lease obligations even if it benefits suppliers.
why_it_matters: Separates AI capex beneficiaries from AI capex cost bearers.
expected_confirming_evidence: Capex/depreciation/leases rise faster than AI/cloud revenue or FCF weakens materially.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: AI/cloud revenue and margin improve enough to absorb capex and depreciation.

claim: Promotional X posts and generic ticker lists should be downweighted in AI industry research packets.
why_it_matters: Prevents keyword spam from contaminating company mapping and report generation.
expected_confirming_evidence: Posts contain promotional group links, no standalone research logic, repeated wording, or ticker stuffing.
expected_disconfirming_evidence: Post contains original analysis, sourceable evidence, and clear investment mechanism despite promotional elements.
